editorial:
Imagine a world where the person you trust most is actually plotting your death. You get pulled into 15th-century England, where Richard, Duke of Gloucester, is tired of waiting his turn for the throne. He is not doing this alone, though. He has a creepy, club-footed executioner named Mord who does all the dirty work. The vibe is dark and tense, feeling more like a scary thriller than a boring history lesson. You will feel the pressure as Richard slowly removes everyone in his way to become the king.

What really makes this work is the acting, especially the way the villains chew the scenery. The pacing is quick, and the twists keep you guessing who will survive the night. While some of the special effects look old now, the drama still hits hard. If you enjoy stories about power and betrayal, you should definitely check this out. It is a great pick for a rainy weekend night.
endingExplained: In the end, Richard finally gets the crown, but his cruelty catches up to him. The people turn against him, and he loses his grip on power. He ends up facing the same fate as the people he killed. Mord, his loyal but scary helper, also meets a grim end. It all wraps up with Richard losing everything just as he thought he had won it all, proving that being a tyrant never ends well.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old school horror and royal scandals.
